facts.text: Its territorial call is a slow, high ah-ah-aaaah with the last note drawn out, given from a prominent perch.
facts.quote: The territorial call of the Australian raven is a slow, high ah-ah-aaaah (similar to the near-open front unrounded vowel (IPA:/æ/)) with the last note drawn out.

facts.text: Flying ravens give a single high-pitched caa over another territory to signal they are just passing through.
facts.quote: Birds in flocks make a single high-pitched caa while flying over another territory as a transit call to signify they are just passing through.

facts.text: Pairs generally bond for life, and if the female dies the male keeps the territory and finds a new mate.
facts.quote: If the female dies, the male Australian raven maintains the territory and finds another mate, while if the male bird is lost, the female abandons the territory.

facts.text: Ravens build a new nest each year, since reusing old ones could spread disease or parasites.
facts.quote: New nests are built each year generally, as the re-use of old ones might spread disease or parasites—nests become caked with faeces as the nestlings grow and the parents cannot keep up with its removal.

facts.text: It thrives in cities such as Sydney, Canberra and Perth, having adapted well to human settlements.
facts.quote: it has adapted well to human settlements and other urban environments, and is a commonly sighted bird in several major cities, including Sydney, Canberra, Perth, Adelaide and Brisbane.

facts.text: Australia's largest corvid, the Australian raven is 46–53 cm long with a 100 cm wingspan and weighs around 650 g.
facts.quote: Measuring 46–53 cm (18–21 in) in length with a 100 cm (39 in) wingspan and weighing around the 650 g (1+7⁄16 lb), the Australian raven is Australia's largest species of corvid.

facts.text: Its eye colour changes with age: young birds have brown irises that turn hazel and later white.
facts.quote: hatchlings and young birds have brown, dark irises until about fifteen months of age, at which point their irises become hazel-coloured

facts.text: Ravens begin breeding at three years of age and live another four to five years on average.
facts.quote: Once they begin breeding at three years of age, they live another four to five years on average.

facts.text: The highest recorded corvid nest in Australia was found on top of the AWA Tower in Sydney.
facts.quote: The highest recorded corvid nest in Australia was found atop the AWA Tower in Sydney.

facts.text: A breeding pair and their brood can hold a territory of up to around 120 hectares all year round.
facts.quote: A single breeding pair and their brood can occupy a territory of up to around 120 hectares (300 acres) and remains there year-round
